name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,524

clue.text: Against stopping revolutionary comrade's vehicular procession

indicators.note: a revolutionary overturns the established order, so the following word's letters are turned about
something stopping a gap plugs it, so this piece is plugged into the middle of the other

blocks.note: the word itself, without the possessive, as anagram fodder
to can mean against, as in back to back or cheek to cheek

explanation.surface: A political radical's cavalcade is being held up by someone opposed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged comrade gives MORCADE, and TO sits after its first two letters to make MOTORCADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcade is a formal procession of cars, so it is literally a parade made up of vehicles.

clue.text: A precocious little girl whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: looking at it from either end gives the same result, which is what a word reading identically both ways does

blocks.note: the definition and the whole of the wordplay at once: the word for a cheeky girl is the same read from either end

explanation.surface: Someone sums up a cheeky child as forward from every angle.
explanation.walkthrough: MADAM reads the same forwards and backwards, so the tail of the clue describes the word's shape rather than giving more letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a pert, forward girl a little madam is an everyday British expression of mild disapproval.

clue.text: Distinctly defined charm associated with Turkey

blocks.note: TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey
to charm someone is to enchant them

explanation.surface: A travel writer links the country of Turkey with a particular kind of allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means vigorous and clear-cut, as in sharply outlined criticism with crisp edges.

clue.text: Daughter entering about to steal something to eat

indicators.note: entering means coming in through the door at the end, so the daughter follows the word for about

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the standard abbreviation for daughter
cabbage is old British slang for pilfering, originally a tailor stealing leftover cloth

explanation.surface: A girl walks in just as someone is about to commit a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: D enters right after RE, coming in at its end to make RED; cabbage meaning steal is a dictionary sense many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Red cabbage is a purple-leaved vegetable, often pickled or braised, so it is edible food.

clue.text: Foolishly crave owning most of his record collection

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving without sense or order, so the following word's letters lose their order
most of a word means all but its final letter is kept
owning something means holding it, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the word with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A fan longs, rather daftly, to possess most of a musician's back catalogue of records.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled crave gives ARCVE, with HI placed after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of documents or records kept for reference and posterity.

clue.text: Catch WWII performers entertaining new soldiers

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to host them, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: ENSA, the Entertainments National Service Association, put on shows for British troops in the Second World War
the standard abbreviation for new
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Wartime entertainers put on a show for freshly recruited troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like it describes the performers' job, but it is the signal to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap or capture, as an animal is caught in a snare.

clue.text: Greatly reduce rent

blocks.note: first meaning: cut prices or costs drastically
second meaning: a long cut or tear, as rent is a split in fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plea to lower housing costs, but rent here is the noun for a tear, not money paid to a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Slash works as a verb for drastic cutting of prices and as a noun for a long gash or tear.

clue.text: Witch doctor dismissing article as false

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so the named letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: a shaman is a tribal healer and spirit-worker
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tribal healer rejects a piece of writing as untrue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sham as an adjective means fake or bogus, something pretending to be genuine.

clue.text: Become apparent in some of Vasari's eccentricities

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are used, a run lying inside the words

blocks.note: the run straddles the possessive and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: An art historian notices that a pattern emerges from the Renaissance biographer Giorgio Vasari's quirks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across vASARI'S Eccentricities, ignoring the apostrophe; Vasari was a sixteenth-century Italian painter and writer on artists.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to emerge or come into view, as problems arise when they show up.

clue.text: Callous as Doris would become after Rex left

definitions.text: as Doris would become after Rex left
definitions.note: a cryptic description of the word read as HEART-LESS

blocks.note: first meaning: cold and unfeeling

blocks.clueFragment: as Doris would become after Rex left
blocks.note: second meaning: the name has R at its centre, so losing R would leave it without its middle letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Doris is left cold and bitter once a man called Rex walks out on her.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is R, the crossword abbreviation for king, and R is the heart of DORIS, so without it she would be heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartless shows no pity or compassion, the same hard, unkind quality as being callous.

clue.text: No longer effective without king becoming an object of fear

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a dead policy or battery no longer works
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch, powerless without his crown, has turned into a figure people fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside: DEAD goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread can name the thing feared itself, as when a disease is called the dread of sailors.

clue.text: Country starts to impose crippling austerity after Castro's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
the starts of the words that follow are the only letters taken
after places the first group of letters later in the answer than the rearranged name

blocks.note: the name without its possessive, as anagram fodder
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A Latin American nation begins harsh cuts after Fidel Castro's radio address.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American republic, so it is a straightforward example of a nation.

clue.text: Automatic for Bottom perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: done without thought, like a machine
second meaning: Bottom the weaver is one of Shakespeare's rude workmen in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.walkthrough: Bottom looks like the backside, but it is the Shakespeare character; the craftsmen who stage the play-within-a-play are called the rude mechanicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanical describes a reflex done without thought, and as a noun it was Shakespeare's term for a manual worker.

clue.text: The French newspaper inclined towards socialism

blocks.note: le is French for the
FT is the Financial Times, a London business daily

explanation.surface: Le Monde is described as a paper with socialist leanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in politics means holding progressive or socialist views, the wing opposed to the right.

clue.text: Throw into confusion with failure to capture gunmen in the centre of Honolulu

indicators.note: only the middle letters of the place name that follows are taken
in places the military unit inside the letters drawn from the place name
capturing something means holding it, so the word for failure surrounds what follows

blocks.note: the demise of a business is its collapse
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners
the two central letters of an eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A failed attempt to seize armed men in downtown Honolulu causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two containers here: the gunners first go inside the middle of Honolulu, then that whole chunk goes inside the failure.
explanation.definitionFit: To demoralise is to dishearten and unsettle someone, knocking their confidence into disarray.

clue.text: Novelist found in dingy island retreat for the most part

indicators.note: the most part of a word is all of it except its final letter
to retreat is to go back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: drab means dull and dreary
Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled

explanation.surface: A writer is discovered hiding out in a shabby island hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: ELBA loses its last letter to ELB, which is turned round; Margaret Drabble is a British novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Drabble wrote The Millstone and many other novels, so she is an example of a fiction writer.

clue.text: Performed gripping song by girl about old farm worker

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it tight, so the first word wraps round the rest
about here means turned around, so the name is read in the other direction

blocks.note: did as in did a play, performed it
an air is a tune or melody
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A singer's stirring ballad about a country lass from olden days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it means concerning the girl, but it turns her name round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairymaid was a woman employed on a farm to milk cows and make butter, a job of the past.

clue.text: Hesitation before Jew needing no introduction becomes a recluse

indicators.note: with no introduction the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
a Semite is a member of a group of peoples including Jews

explanation.surface: A pause before a famous Jewish figure, so well known they need no introduction, turns into withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious hermit, someone who lives alone apart from society.

clue.text: At home getting a couple of texts after a former president turned up dead

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so the name runs backwards
a couple means two, so only the first two letters of the word are kept
after puts the two kept letters later than the rest of the wordplay

blocks.note: in means at home, as in staying in
taken as written
Idi Amin was president of Uganda in the 1970s
the first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone at home receives a couple of messages after a former head of state is found dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means without life, like a stone, which is what dead describes.

clue.text: One for example discovered in oddly neglected hedge in Bury

indicators.note: neglecting the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones
in sets the kept letters inside the word for burying

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
to inter is to bury a body

explanation.surface: Something turns up in an overgrown hedge in Bury, the Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is capitalised to look like the town near Manchester, but it is the verb meaning to put in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The number one is a whole number, so it is an example of an integer.

clue.text: Unrestrained bombast overwhelming American politician

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf completely, so one piece swallows the others

blocks.note: a rant is loud, overblown talk
the standard abbreviation for American
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Wild ranting drowns out a US politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means running wild and unchecked, as rampant inflation is out of control.

clue.text: Virginia looking into good health in retirement exhibited by southern Europeans

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the toast is read backwards
looking into a place puts you inside it, so the state goes into the other word
exhibited by sets the following letter alongside the rest of the wordplay

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for southern
skol is a Scandinavian drinking toast, like cheers
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman called Virginia drinks to good health in her retirement among southern European friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia looks like a woman's name but is the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovaks are the people of Slovakia, a country in central Europe, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: Be seen assembled outside home in which spirits may be found

definitions.text: in which spirits may be found
definitions.note: a description of a place; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: something assembled is built up from parts, so these letters are put together in a new order
outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
H is the abbreviation for home

explanation.surface: Ghosts gather to be seen around a haunted house.
explanation.walkthrough: The spirits sound supernatural but they are alcohol; a shebeen is an unlicensed drinking den in Ireland, Scotland or South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an illicit bar selling drink, so liquor like whisky and gin is found inside one.

clue.text: Means to go west on large boat

indicators.note: going west in an across entry means running right to left, so the word is read backwards
on means placed next to, so one piece joins the other

blocks.note: a way is a method or means of doing something
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A traveller's way of heading west is aboard a big ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel, or a ship's small rowing boat.

clue.text: Going after valuables originally missing from vehicle

indicators.note: with what was there originally missing, the word loses its first letter
after places the first word later in the answer than what follows it

blocks.note: swag is slang for stolen goods or valuables
on as in the machine is on, working or going

explanation.surface: A thief returns for loot that has gone missing from a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like an adverb about when things went missing, but it means the first letter of swag is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a four-wheeled cart or railway truck used for carrying goods, so it is a vehicle.

clue.text: Crucial as Poins is in effect loveless

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, an O, so being loveless means that letter is taken away

blocks.note: Poins is the setter, who would say I am
a law that is operative is in force, in effect

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being essential while admitting to a life without love.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters use their pseudonym for I or me, so Poins is becomes I'M; Poins is also a crony of Prince Hal in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperative means absolutely necessary or vital, the same sense as calling a matter crucial.

clue.text: Make a strenuous effort to disregard hint of presumption in scientific witness

indicators.note: a hint is a small trace, so only the opening letter of the word is taken
disregarding something means leaving it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: an expert witness gives specialist evidence in court
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A forensic witness in court works hard not to presume anything.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert yourself is to apply force or energy, pushing hard at a task.

clue.text: Heroism without support? Absolutely

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named item is taken out of the word

blocks.note: bravery is courage
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether courage counts if no one backs you up, and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAVERY loses BRA from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Very used as an adverb intensifies, meaning extremely or completely, just as absolutely does.

clue.text: Collective anger essentially admitted by chief in time

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter is taken
being admitted means let in, so that letter goes inside the next word
in places the second word inside the word for time

blocks.note: the centre of a five-letter word
great can mean principal or chief, as in the great hall
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A group's fury is acknowledged by the leader in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the core of anger goes inside the word for chief, and that goes inside the word for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate means combined or total, formed by gathering separate parts into a single whole.

clue.text: That's assuming grandma is unimaginative

indicators.note: to assume a role is to take it on, so the first piece takes the second within itself

blocks.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that presuming an old lady lacks creativity is a given.
explanation.walkthrough: That's reads as a contraction, but it is that is, abbreviated i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and empty of sense, close to the dull, uninspired quality of unimaginative.

clue.text: Old Penny Black is small and neat

blocks.note: d was the symbol for a penny in British money before 1971, from the Latin denarius
inky means dark as ink

explanation.surface: A collector notes that the famous Penny Black stamp is compact and tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Penny Black was the first postage stamp, issued in Britain in 1840, but the clue splits the two words apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinky is a British informal word meaning cute and compact, like Dinky toy cars.

clue.text: Most sympathetic loan provider initially ignored during trial

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word
something ignored is left out, so that letter is removed
during means within the span of, so the shortened word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a lender provides loans
the opening letter
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: The most understanding bank turns out to be the one that skipped a credit check.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderest is the superlative of tender, meaning gentle and caring, so it means the most compassionate.
